# Decisions And Constraints

<!-- Generated by repo-harness-builder; source: core/docs:3.0 -->

## Standing Decisions
<!-- doc-role:standing-decisions -->

- Repository documentation remains the visible source of project state.
- `repo-harness` is a repository-scoped system of prompts, guardrails, harness rules, durable documentation, skills, and commands that strengthens and assists AI coding agents such as OpenCode, Claude Code, and Pi. `repo-harness-builder` creates, audits, installs, and safely evolves that system inside a selected repository. The harness is independently useful in standalone mode and may use optional ecosystem components according to the selected integration mode. Gentle AI is the broader routing, review, receipts, and delivery ecosystem; Engram provides semantic continuity without replacing repository truth; and CodeGraph is the most optional repository-local code intelligence and navigation aid, never an authority store. Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, and Pi are inspiration sources only, not dependencies or products this project recreates.
- A claim is a verified fact only when applicable, trustworthy, and proportionate evidence supports it. Supported inferences state their evidence and reasoning; claims without a valid mechanism remain unknown or unverifiable; and human decisions are requested only when authority or a criterion belongs to a person. Missing evidence, stale memory, unrelated proxies, assumptions, and confidence wording never substitute for verification. Available verification runs before asking; when it is unavailable or contradictory, the workflow names the missing capability and requests only the minimum evidence, criterion, authority, or decision.
- Git, GitHub, issues, pull requests, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, Gentle AI, Engram, CodeGraph, provider tooling, and similar integrations are optional. Absence or failure degrades only the capability each integration owns and never permits a Git-backed guarantee when Git is unavailable. Git is highly recommended because it improves history, diff, recovery, rollback, branches, commits, and delivery safety. Without Git, give one useful warning or recommendation that Git is the preferred minimum for full safety, then continue supported non-Git operation without refusal or repeated prompting.
- Editable product sources are `skill/repo-harness-builder/` and `command/repo-harness-builder.md`; `.claude/`, `.opencode/`, and `.pi/` are selected-runtime projections for execution and testing.
- Every selected runtime carries repository-local copies of the operational skills its entry surfaces invoke. Claude Code and OpenCode retain command entry surfaces, Pi retains prompt entry surfaces, and all three use the same canonical skill bodies with only the existing `canonical-source:` provenance normalization. Runtime-family syntax never justifies a dependency on a global skill registry.
- This repository reciprocally develops `repo-harness-builder` and runs its generated `repo-harness` against the same product source as a self-hosting proving ground. Complete parity here therefore includes each selected runtime's exact builder package projection, its family-specific callable builder entry, all three generated operational skills, and their entries. The optional authenticated `canonicalProjections` manifest field records exact product projections only when canonical builder sources are present; ordinary consumer manifests omit it. Self-hosted repository policy is evidence, not generic product behavior by default.
- Before release, every relevant behavior is classified as builder-only scaffolding, repository-specific policy, or generic consumer contract. Release requires the generic consumer contract to produce an operational, correct, functional, recoverable, and self-improving harness for any project type, operating system, and compatible agent. The evidence discipline above governs that classification; this decision does not duplicate it.
- If Git exists but the selected folder is not initialized, offer initialization only after explicit human approval. Provider publication remains an optional, separately approved boundary and requires an explicit private or public visibility choice.
- New or effectively empty repositories receive a complete useful baseline after plan approval, including `README.md`. Existing repositories receive content analysis and an informed integration proposal. Obsolete or incompatible content may be archived for a clean baseline only after a distinct conversational choice and explicit approval.
- Generated ownership markers may bound generated material but never exempt a pre-existing README or other human-owned document from analysis and improvement.
- Only an explicitly active `repo-harness-builder` skill execution uses strict language-scoped digest-bound tokens for its content-bound apply plan: English `APPROVE` or `DENY`, Spanish `APROBAR` or `DENEGAR`. Apply requires both digest and exact token. Direct CLI calls default to English, and language never enters the plan digest. Repository identity, self-hosting, ordinary repository maintenance, generated-file ownership, session skills, and direct questions do not activate this interface. Outside an active builder skill execution, approval remains conversational.
- That boundary is enforced by the CLI, not by prose alone. `render` takes `--activation builder|maintenance` and defaults to `maintenance`, which omits `approvalPrompt` and `approvalAnswers` from its output entirely, rejects `--approval`, and applies on the matching digest alone. The reason is that a preview which always printed the strict envelope handed every caller a ready-to-relay approval interface, so the contract said one thing and the tool did another. An interface that must not exist outside one execution must not be emitted outside it either. The plan digest is identical under both activations.
- Root runtime pointers preserve all existing bytes, detect the exact directive as a complete line, and append only the missing newline-delimited directive using the existing consistent line-ending convention where possible.
- Prior harness versions are audited rather than refused because managed files exist. Upgrade analysis classifies current, stale, missing, human-evolved, and legacy paths. Replacement, archive, and deletion require an exact proposed action and explicit user approval.
- Existing current-version generated outputs may be replaced only when an authenticated installed manifest/checker pair proves the exact owned path and the current bytes retain generated provenance. This includes human modifications retaining a valid current-version marker. Preview binds path, action kind, exact source and destination SHA-256 values, and plan digest; apply rejects post-preview edits and rolls back every create, append, and replacement on failure. Human-owned, human-evolved, legacy, and unverifiable paths remain proposal-only. Desired checker bytes must match the desired manifest digest, and a changed valid pair is replaced atomically.
- An installed harness must be updatable in one pass. A builder version bump may not freeze the installations it exists to update, so replacement authority follows builder provenance rather than exact version equality, and a two-pass repair is not an acceptable update path. A path without builder provenance stays human-owned and proposal-only regardless. No consumer repository is ever modified to unblock the builder, and this repository plans no work inside one: installing and running a release is the owner's action, not a task this repository schedules.
- Generated session-stop approvals are resumable checkpoints within the same invocation. Approved actions run once, declined documentation does not stop closing, and final handoff output follows refreshed evidence and successful final continuity saving.
- Generated session-start synchronizes only after read-only state inspection and conversational outcome approval. Explicit safe-sync intent covers bounded fetch and fast-forward-only integration while facts remain unchanged, never blind pull, rebase, reset, or automatic conflict resolution.
- Generated session-stop completes documentation and continuity before Git. Consent is outcome-scoped: combined commit-and-push intent covers exact staging, one read-only staged-scope check, commit, checks, one fetch preflight, and one push to the identified upstream. The staged check compares workflow path names and status/modes with the approved work unit while keeping pre-existing staged work separate. A mismatch invalidates consent; selective unstage is allowed only when it cannot disturb pre-existing staged work. Commit-only and push-only stay narrow. Material scope, sensitivity, remote, destination, credential, integration, hook, or verification changes invalidate consent.
- Generated sessions use scoped `ready`, `paused`, `blocked`, `failed`, `completed`, and `degraded` outcomes. Required continuity and optional Git branches report separately, and optional Git failure never falsely fails the whole session.
- Every safe pending approval is one concrete final question. Commit proposals require per-path sensitive screening, exact work-unit paths, rationale, Conventional Commit message, exclusions, and staged-path disclosure. Transport diagnostics retain bounded command receipts and safely-local state.
- Self-hosted verification separates on-disk projection parity from active-process registered skill freshness and from runtime reload capability. Same-process stale registered content degrades only optional live validation; it does not block or fail verified repository state, documentation close, or continuity, and no reload command is assumed.
- Spanish generated docs use complete natural templates rather than chained heading replacement. The checker combines locale-independent semantic roles with proportional required-phrase and known-leakage baselines; it detects missing required content but does not pretend automated checks prove semantic equivalence.
- Declared documentation locales and the conversation language control generated runtime help routing, so the help wrapper can only name a guide the same render creates. The report language is presentational and changes no generated byte, so the action-plan digest stays identical across report languages with no normalization.
- README selector integration is atomic. When an existing `README.md` lacks the reciprocal Spanish link and no approved existing-file integration action is executable, `README.es.md` is blocked and the whole apply fails closed. Executable existing-file integration remains a broader pending capability.
- Repository contributions are issue-first, use short focused branches and linked PRs, follow Conventional Commits, keep tests and docs in the same work unit, and require maintainer review before merge. Direct changes to `main` require an explicit maintainer emergency; approval is conversational because this repository has no custom contribution labels, templates, or automated approval gate.
- `docs/repo-harness/roadmap.md` is the canonical lifecycle owner for non-trivial pending and resolved work. Immutable `RH-W-####` records use justified priority and controlled status; `current-state.md` is only the active projection, localized peers mirror the owner, and Engram topic `work/RH-W-####` mirrors outcomes without owning the backlog.
- Human repository documentation supports English-only, Spanish-only, and bilingual declarations. Monolingual output uses canonical paths; bilingual output keeps English canonical owners plus complete Spanish peers. Skills, contracts, wrappers, checker machinery, manifest instructions and schema, code, comments, runtime instructions, and technical artifacts stay in English. This separates human reading surfaces from machine-facing contracts instead of forcing English ownership onto both domains.
- Blocking language decisions are resumable transitions: after each answer, the builder immediately emits the next required question in the next turn and stops again. It never waits for filler input or combines two blocking questions.
- What the agent reads and what the agent says to the user are separate choices. Documentation locales govern available reading surfaces and default to English only; guide locale never determines reply language. Conversation language follows a current verified explicit human instruction, then persisted explicit preference, established verified session language only without persisted preference, validated manifest fallback, and deterministic English. Only a later verified explicit human instruction changes persisted preference. Ordinary prose and contextual bytes are not switch evidence, and language resolution never changes machine-significant bytes or permission scope.
- Self-hosted owner render, preview, and apply commands always pass the installed runtime set, license, report language, documentation locales, and conversation language explicitly. The authenticated manifest retains the selected generated-skill license because it is the smallest trusted state from which canonical builder `check()` can reproduce expected bytes for non-MIT installations; arbitrary installed skill bytes never supply it. Authenticated historical manifests without that field retain unknown license authority and cannot select or replace license-dependent bytes until the owner supplies the trusted license explicitly; that authorized upgrade keeps the manifest/checker pair atomic. Generated-checker parity proves consistency with the installed manifest; it does not replace an explicit owner-render idempotence check.
- Every generated repository protects the checker and manifest exact-byte contract through only `.repo-harness/check.py text eol=lf` and `.repo-harness/manifest.json text eol=lf` in root `.gitattributes`. Existing human attributes remain byte-preserved, missing exact rules append through the approved content-bound plan, and conflicting matching rules block before writes. No repository-wide line-ending policy is imposed.
- Capability-aware coordination preserves owner boundaries. The repository owns durable truth, source and tests, policy, backlog, and approvals. Gentle AI and Engram are independent optional capabilities that compose independently, without a named paired mode, third state machine, or copied authority. Gentle AI optionally owns routing, exact-candidate review and receipts, and delivery gates when enabled. Engram optionally owns semantic memory, relations and conflicts, review-age metadata, and session continuity. Completed RH-W-0025 retains the detector classifications `not_found`, `found_on_path`, and `verified`; `available`, `unavailable`, `partial`, `disabled`, and contextual `policy-required` are distinct effective states derived for the requested operation, not detector classifications. Absence or failure causes operation-scoped degradation only for behavior owned by that capability unless repository policy requires it for that operation.
- Harness Engram operations require explicit project scope. Engram is semantic continuity, not authority for backlog, approval, delivery, classification, reconciliation, repository state, source, tests, or human decisions.
- Engram results remain operation-level evidence, not one available, degraded, or absent verdict. Report project resolution, local read, local write, prompt association, conflict discovery, lifecycle review, plugin capture, and sync independently when applicable. A successful observation save remains successful if best-effort prompt capture or post-save conflict-candidate discovery fails.
- Conflict candidates are advisory. `judgment_required` means candidate relations were produced and does not establish contradiction. `active` and `needs_review` are computed review-age labels based on `review_after`, not truth, verification, authority, expiry, or deletion states.
- OpenCode plugin capture, automatic prompt capture, compaction handoff, and passive capture are best-effort channels whose success requires evidence. Engram's current SQLite local-first implementation is a verified implementation detail, not a harness-mandated dependency; future compatible implementations may preserve the contract through another supported local boundary.
- Durable reusable discoveries are promoted selectively to the correct canonical repository owner only after human approval. External facts that can change are labeled current and revalidated before reuse; incidental noise is not persisted. Generated consumer harnesses never mention improving `repo-harness-builder`; this self-hosted repository applies the same generic contract to its own product source. Coordination never auto-enables review, fabricates approval, creates synthetic SDD, duplicates lifecycle, receipt, or conflict stores, or loops until clean.
- Gentle AI is detected only through bounded, shell-free PATH execution of `gentle-ai version`, not through installation layout. Process creation failure is `not_found`; timeout, nonzero exit, or malformed output is `found_on_path`; only exit 0 with normalized `gentle-ai <version>` output is `verified`. Engram installation preflight uses evidence from the host's supported MCP or CLI boundary, never unrelated files or memory content; runtime continuity then preserves the independent operation outcomes defined above. Integrated selection, approval, and apply require verified evidence for both components and preserve both component results on refusal. Executing a PATH binary is not read-only in the strict security sense, but it is the same trust level the harness already extends to `git` and `python`.
- Merged branches are deleted, and `deleteBranchOnMerge` is enabled on the repository so GitHub removes the head branch automatically. Deleting a merged branch loses nothing: the commits stay reachable from `main`, and GitHub preserves the pull request with its branch name, diff, commits, and conversation permanently. Branches are kept only while unmerged, long-running, or referenced by something external. On 2026-08-15 the setting was off and 16 stale branches had accumulated; they were deleted after verifying each was merged, and `docs/record-optional-codegraph` was deleted only after its `RH-W-0026` record was confirmed byte-identical on `main`.
- A rule the agent must follow internally is not enforced until the output contract requires it to be visible. `REPO-HARNESS.md` classifies every claim as verified fact, supported inference, unknown or unverifiable, or human decision required, and the daily Output Contracts now require that class to appear in the report itself, an inference to name the evidence it rests on and what would raise it to verified, and never to be presented in assertive form. This is a strengthened obligation, not a gate: `check.py` compares bytes and cannot enforce a prose rule about prose output, so it is defended by review rather than by exit code.
- Position is not visibility. `.repo-harness/rules/response-contract.md` is the sole complete owner of the blocked-question and informational next-action syntax, including delimiter forms, labels, setext safety, and when no block is appropriate. Each daily Output Contract carries only the concise reference that applies this owner to the agent's reply and reported output. The rule remains review-enforced because `check.py` compares bytes and cannot judge prose output.
- Announcing executable work is not follow-through. When a verification or action is immediately executable inside the requested and authorized scope, the agent executes it and reports the result rather than stopping after the announcement. It pauses only for approval, authority, evidence, safety, or a material decision. This general rule belongs in `REPO-HARNESS.md`; it does not authorize unrequested tasks, reuse approval, or weaken any authority boundary, and it does not reopen the visual discoverability scope owned by `RH-W-0058`.
- User-owned personal storage is outside the harness boundary. Generated contracts and canonical product documentation neither name nor depend on its paths. Harness-owned local state belongs under `.repo-harness/` by default.
- The owner-approved and implemented RH-W-0051 design assigns disposable state to `.repo-harness/tmp/`, recoverable archives to `.repo-harness/archive/`, small declared consumer state to `.repo-harness/state/`, and local session backups to `.repo-harness/memory-bk/`. All are non-authoritative and Git-ignored by default. Archive and memory backups are never automatically deleted initially. The verified implementation declares and checks the taxonomy without adding consumer behavior.
- Documentation is canonical durable truth by domain; memory is operational continuity. Engram and local backups are cross-checked non-authoritative evidence, never duplicate documentation, lifecycle, approval, conflict, receipt, or delivery stores. Current repository evidence resolves claims before memory is trusted, and unresolved material decisions return to the human.
- Finding reconciliation is a harness responsibility. Before routing next work, it inventories findings, classifies each as integrate, close, defer, reject, or noise, reconciles canonical, localized, and memory evidence, promotes only with approval, and cleans stale or duplicate continuity without blindly deleting history. Post-delivery performs the same lifecycle reconciliation and recommends the next ready unit.
- The owner-approved `RH-W-0050` design adopts hybrid activation: every start and qualifying stop performs a deterministic bounded scan, while an explicit full request or verified mandatory evidence triggers full reconciliation inside the bounded owner scope. Repository evidence remains authoritative, Engram operations remain explicitly project-scoped and independently reported, advisory metadata never proves contradiction, and implementation may add no duplicate backlog, cache, receipt, ledger, trigger state, or lifecycle store. The [design owner](rh-w-0050-design.md) defines the exact bounds, triggers, result states, authority, RED/GREEN matrix, and implementation impact. Approval of that design does not authorize or claim implementation.
- The owner approved the revised execution order on 2026-08-21: completed `RH-W-0050` as baseline, then `RH-W-0054`, `RH-W-0011`, the shared local-state design and its separate implementation sequence, followed by the unchanged later units recorded in the roadmap. On 2026-08-22 the owner narrowly scheduled `RH-W-0057` immediately after `RH-W-0054` and before `RH-W-0011`; the remainder stayed unchanged. On 2026-08-23 the owner separately approved its complete design and then explicitly authorized implementation. RH-W-0057 completed test-first the same day, so `RH-W-0011` returns to the next scheduled position.
- This repository is self-contained. Its rules, evidence, history, and pending work live inside this folder, and no workflow here reads, depends on, or schedules work in another repository, workspace, or personal storage. The folder it happens to sit inside is not a repository and is not an authority over it. Historical facts about where the product came from may be recorded, but a pointer that sends a reader outside to recover reasoning is not an acceptable substitute for recording that reasoning here.
- Version control is the safety net. The builder is not presented as a boundary against a hostile filesystem, and its guarantees assume a repository that can revert.
- Runtime selection is never inferred. A runtime set is never derived from surfaces found on disk; the CLI takes a repeatable `--runtime` form, and naming a runtime set is itself the permission to plan.
- Tool-owned path boundary. The builder claims no path under `.atl/`, `.codegraph/`, or `.engram/`. Its only ignore-file behavior is the approved exact root `.codegraph/` directive.
- The entire harness is LLM-first, always. Markdown, rules, skills, commands, state contracts, and runtime instructions optimize for semantic clarity, imperative instructions, discoverability, bounded context, exact machine tokens, explicit precedence, and cross-runtime LLM portability. Human readability remains important, but no human-oriented convention may make the LLM contract ambiguous. `RH-W-0084` owns establishing, by measurement rather than by assertion, what that actually means for formats, sizes, paths, reinforcement, and forms.
- Project charter. This is the standing essence of every change made here, recorded once so no unit has to rediscover it: LLM-first and organic; proportionality with no overengineering; stay inside the selected repository unless leaving it is strictly necessary; never assume, and never state a claim as more certain than its evidence; verify and review, because the data and the code decide; solve the real present problem rather than an imagined future one; evidence before supposition; an adaptive harness that improves itself within bounded scope; documentation as a first-class deliverable rather than an afterthought, kept canonical, localized, and reconciled in the same work unit as the change it describes; recursive self-hosting, so the builder is always exercised on itself; honesty with explicit limits; a human in the loop for every authority decision; ask with the required visible form; and never end a reply without a next step that actually makes sense. This entry is a charter, not a new rule: every principle keeps its existing owner. `REPO-HARNESS.md` owns the never-miss rules, `.repo-harness/rules/working-agreements.md` owns sizing, stopping, and proportionality, `.repo-harness/rules/response-contract.md` owns the question and next-action forms, and the roadmap owns lifecycle. Nothing here creates duplicate policy or raises any budget.
- User presentation preferences use one ignored structured Markdown contract at `.repo-harness/state/preferences/user-preferences.md`, never generated bytes or tracked personal values. Its three independent axes remain separately owned: RH-W-0071 `response-structure`, RH-W-0082 `explanation-style`, and RH-W-0018 `interaction-behavior`, with RH-W-0046 retaining consent boundaries, RH-W-0051 retaining containment, RH-W-0067 retaining the complete response contract, and RH-W-0031 retaining language provenance. The prior unimplemented JSON scalar contract is superseded without a data-migration claim.
- Generated session-start must not delegate to a subagent. The purpose of session-start is to load evidence into the main thread, and a subagent compresses and returns a summary, which discards the exact evidence the parent needs. Delegation exists to keep noise out of the parent; here the evidence is the point.
- A capability preflight reports the classification it decided, never the evidence it decided from. The host supplies its own Engram evidence, so printing that object back publishes whatever payload it happened to carry, and the same applies to a tool's captured stdout and stderr. `detect_gentle_ai()` and `detect_engram()` keep the complete evidence internally because the verification needs it; `capability_projection()` removes it from every printed surface. This narrowed a shipped `RH-W-0025` output: the failed-closed report no longer includes per-component evidence, and the contract test that asserted the full object now asserts the classification it was really about.
